title: Episode 01 — What a lobbying database can and cannot prove
footer: THE SENTINEL REPORT · WE WATCH THE CODE
_production: Built from the Senate LDA capture library on this machine. Every number
comes from data/graph_counts.json, which is the printed output of
`bin/sentinel connect graph`.
BEFORE PUBLISHING, RE-RUN THE GRAPH. These counts have already moved once
— see _why_this_file_shrank in data/graph_counts.json. If they move again,
update that file, re-hash it into the final scene, and re-render. Paste the
WHOLE graph output, not the lines you happen to need, or the file ends up
mixing two runs and cannot be audited against either:
bin/sentinel connect graph
shasum -a 256 data/graph_counts.json     # paste into the hash scene
python3 ../../engine/openmontage.py --spec episode.json --check-safe
python3 ../../engine/openmontage.py --spec episode.json --out builds/ep01.mp4
The build REFUSES to render if the hash and the file disagree, which is
how you find out you forgot.
WHY THIS EPISODE IS SHAPED AS A REFUSAL: the graph tool already prints the
distinction between a sworn filing and a search result, and warns that
every count is a floor. That restraint is the story. An episode that
showed the big number and skipped the caveat would be the ordinary version
of this video, and it would be worth less.
4 scenes are yours on camera.
PHOTOS: none yet. See ../../docs/SHOTLIST.md and ../../docs/VISUAL_POLICY.md
— every photo scene needs `origin` and a credit.

scenes.title: We captured 5,688 pages of the lobbying register.
scenes.sub: Then we spent most of the work deciding what they do not prove.
scenes.vo: We pulled the federal lobbying register. Most of the work was deciding what it doesn't show.
scenes.delivery: Flat. The number is not the boast — the second line is the point.

scenes.question: What can a database actually prove?

scenes.caption: filings that assert a relationship.
scenes.sub: A registrant swore, in a filing, that it lobbied for a named client. That is a fact on a form, and it is the strongest thing in the set.
scenes.vo: Five thousand and fifty-two sworn filings. Someone put their name to each one. That is the strong material.
scenes.delivery: Confident. This is the number you can stand behind.

scenes.caption: search results that prove nothing.
scenes.sub: Two companies came back from the same query. That is a coincidence of names, not a connection between them — and there are nearly twice as many of these as the real thing.
scenes.vo: Nearly nine thousand search results. Two firms answering one query is not a link between them.
scenes.delivery: This is the turn. Slow down and let the contrast land.

scenes.label: THE RULE
scenes.quote: Two companies under the same subject are two hops apart. There is no edge between them.
scenes.source: Source: sentinel connect graph, preview output, captured library
scenes.vo: So the tool refuses to draw the line. The eye reads a line as a fact, and the captures do not establish one.
scenes.delivery: The thesis of the episode. Slower than everything around it.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — verbatim from the graph preview output.

scenes.question: Why not just draw the line anyway?
scenes.source_note: Host scene. Film yourself here. The honest answer is the whole brand.

scenes.caption: captures held fewer rows than the source reported.
scenes.sub: So every number in this episode is a minimum, not a total. The nodes carry counts_are_floors: true, and the graph says so before it says anything else.
scenes.vo: Thirty-seven hundred captures came back short. So every number here is a floor, not a total.
scenes.delivery: Matter-of-fact. This is a limitation, stated as one.

scenes.label: WHAT WE WILL NOT DO
scenes.quote: Income and expenses are separate fields and are never added.
scenes.source: Source: sentinel connect graph, money and time on 5,052 filing relationships
scenes.vo: The register reports income and expenses separately. Adding them would produce a bigger number and a false one. So the tool will not do it.
scenes.delivery: Almost throwaway. The restraint should sound routine, because it is.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — verbatim from the graph preview output.

scenes.question: So where does that leave the story?

scenes.title: A place to look. Never a link.
scenes.sub: A search hit tells you where to file a records request. It does not tell you what happened in a room, and the filing does not either.
scenes.vo: A hit tells you where to look next. It never tells you what happened in the room.
scenes.delivery: Hard cut in. Say it once and stop.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — the standing caution printed with every connector run.

scenes.question: What are you requesting first?
scenes.source_note: Host scene. Film yourself here. This is the hook into episode 02.

scenes.title: Every number in this episode is in one file.
scenes.sub: Change one digit and this build refuses to render rather than show a hash the file does not have.
scenes.vo: Every figure is in one file, and its hash is on screen. If they disagree, the video is not made.
scenes.delivery: Close it out. Let the hash finish typing before you stop.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — verified against data/graph_counts.json at build time.
